behaviour.rule: FallbackChain( Retry( CircuitBreaker( RateLimiter( Timeout( Bulkhead( Fault( operation ))))))): the primary stage is the whole inner pipeline; fallback stages run plain with their own optional timeout.
Retry does not retry rejections, so an open circuit goes straight to the fallback; a rejection inside the breaker does not count against it.
validate(value) runs inside the pipeline; a failing (or throwing) check is MalformedPayloadError, counted by the breaker and retried.

Each invocation of the operation asks the FaultInjector for one fault. error/drop throw ChaosError; latency sleeps then runs; timeout hangs until the Timeout layer cancels; truncate halves strings, arrays and bytes (else mutate, else ChaosError); malformed returns mutate's output or MALFORMED_MARKER (Rust: mutate, else MalformedPayload).
With no fallbacks the primary's error is returned as is; with fallbacks that all fail, AllStagesFailedError lists primary first.

After each call the pipeline's report is: healthy when the primary served and the circuit is closed; degraded when a fallback served or the circuit is not closed; error when nothing served. errorCount counts calls whose primary failed; lastErrorCode is the primary error's code; source is primary, the stage, or none.
System health is the worst report: error > degraded > loading > healthy; none → loading.
Reports and events carry codes and numbers only: no error messages, URLs or payloads.

mzizi-resilience.cases.json drives the pipeline on a virtual clock with an explicit fault schedule: faults open the breaker, the fallback serves, health is degraded, the cooldown passes, a half-open probe succeeds, health is healthy again.

gaps: Python lands in phase 2 (mzizi-registry#472): a .py sibling, the /v1/py/{name} route in mzizi-api-gateway and a PyPI package.
The React health panel is the registry item mzizi-health-panel and the section wrapper is mzizi-section (both .tsx); their Astro shells land in phase 3.
Rust has no shared global monitor or subscriptions: a pipeline reports to its own HealthMonitor or an Rc<RefCell<HealthMonitor>> you share; the TS build defaults to the shared healthMonitor.
Seeded random chaos (ChaosEngine) is N8's; this contract defines only the hook it implements.
